subject: ela
skillName: Ask and answer about a speaker

items.prompt:
A classmate says: 'I have a new puppy named Biscuit.' What is a good question to ask for MORE information?
A) 'What is your teacher's name?'
B) 'What kind of dog is Biscuit?'
items.answer: B) 'What kind of dog is Biscuit?'

steps: Option B asks about the puppy the classmate mentioned — it connects to what the speaker said and gathers more information.

items.prompt:
A classmate says something you did not hear clearly. What should you do?
A) Pretend you heard it
B) Ask him to repeat what he said
items.answer: B) Ask him to repeat what he said

steps: Asking a speaker to repeat or clarify something you did not understand is a good listening skill.

items.prompt:
A student talks about her trip to the zoo. She says she saw an animal called a 'tapir' but you do not know what that is. What question should you ask?
A) 'What is a tapir?'
B) 'What is your favorite color?'

steps: If you do not understand a word the speaker used, ask for clarification about that word.

items.prompt:
A teacher explains how to make a sandwich. After she is done, a student asks: 'What do you put on the sandwich first?' Is this a good question?
A) Yes — it asks about what the speaker explained.
B) No — it has nothing to do with the topic.

steps: The question relates directly to what the teacher was explaining (how to make a sandwich). It asks for more detail about the steps.

items.prompt:
A classmate says: 'I went to my grandma's house this weekend.' What is a good question to learn more?
A) 'Where does your grandma live?'
B) 'Do you like hamburgers?'

steps: Option A asks for more detail about what the classmate said. Option B is off-topic.

items.prompt:
A student presents about their favorite book. She says: 'My favorite book is about a brave little mouse.' What question gives you MORE information?
A) 'What is the mouse's name?'
B) 'Do you like cats?'

steps: Option A asks about a detail directly related to what the speaker said (the mouse in the book).

items.prompt:
A speaker uses the word 'migrate' and you are not sure what it means. What is the best thing to do?
A) Ignore it
B) Ask: 'What does migrate mean?'

steps: When a speaker uses a word you do not understand, asking for clarification is the right move.

items.prompt:
A classmate says: 'I made a craft out of clay. It was really hard to shape it.' What question gets MORE information about what she did?
A) 'What did you make out of clay?'
B) 'What is your favorite movie?'
items.answer: A) 'What did you make out of clay?'

steps: Option A connects to the speaker's craft project. Option B changes the subject entirely.

items.prompt:
True or False: A good question after a speaker talks should be about what the speaker said.
A) True
B) False

steps: Questions asked about a speaker should connect to what that speaker said — either to clarify or to get more information.

items.prompt:
A classmate says: 'I built a birdhouse with my dad.' A student asks: 'Did you paint it?' Is this a good question?
A) Yes — it asks for more detail about the speaker's project.
B) No — it is rude.

steps: The question asks about a detail (painting) connected to the speaker's birdhouse project — it is a good follow-up question.

items.prompt:
A teacher says: 'We are going on a field trip next Friday.' A student asks: 'Where are we going?' Is this a good question?
A) Yes
B) No

steps: The teacher mentioned a field trip but did not say where. Asking 'where' gathers more specific information about what the speaker said.

items.prompt:
A visitor says she is a nurse. A student asks: 'What do nurses do?' Is this a good question?
A) Yes — it asks the speaker to explain her job.
B) No — nurses and children should not talk.

steps: Asking a speaker to explain or elaborate on what she said (or what she does) is a great question for gathering more information.

items.prompt:
After a classmate finishes talking about soccer, a student asks: 'How many players are on a soccer team?' Is this related to what the speaker said?
A) Yes
B) No

steps: The classmate talked about soccer, so questions about soccer are connected to the speaker's topic.

items.prompt:
A speaker says: 'I want to be an astronaut someday.' You want to know more. Which question is BEST?
A) 'Why do you want to be an astronaut?'
B) 'What did you eat for breakfast?'
items.answer: A) 'Why do you want to be an astronaut?'

steps: Option A asks the speaker to explain her goal — it connects directly to what she said and seeks more information.

items.prompt:
True or False: You should ask a question about a speaker ONLY if you did not understand anything at all.
A) True
B) False

steps: You can ask questions even when you understood the speaker — to get MORE information, learn more details, or explore the topic further.
